The Petitioners in MVC No.926/2022 and MVC No.927/2022 have filed these petitions u/Sec.166 of MV Act  SCCH - 25 3 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
 927/2022 seeking compensation for the death of their son Mr.Venkatesh and for the injuries sustained by him in an RTA.

Both the petitions arose out of a common accident,
therefore both the petitions are clubbed together as per order dated 14.03.2023, common evidence is recorded and common judgment is passed.
2. The case of the Petitioners in both the cases is that:

On 31.10.2021 at about 7.30pm, Mr.Venkatesh and V.G.Mahesh were proceeding in the motorcycle bearing No.AP-02-CC-4368 as rider and pillion rider, following all traffic rules, a Lorry bearing No.KA-51-AA-8042 without Vadde Narayanamma vs K. Sunitha on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148025627/
2 following the traffic rules and also not applying the parking light and any precaution was parked in the Center of the road.
At that time the rider of the motorcycle hit the back side of the Lorry, due to impact both rider and pillion rider got injured.

It is the further case of the Petitioners in MVC No.926/2022 that, immediately after the accident deceased was shifted to Madakshira Government Hospital, provided first aid then shifted to NIMHANS, Bangalore, finally shifted him to Madu Hospital, Dasarahalli, Bangalore.
The Doctor operated on the head injury and Mr.Venkatesh died on 27.11.2021 and the post mortem was conducted, body handed over to the petitioners.
So far the petitioners have spent Rs.7,00,000/- towards conveyance, food and nourishment charges, funeral and obsequies ceremonies and other incidental charges.
At the time of accident, the deceased Venkatesh was doing Mason Work and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earning towards his family needs and welfare.
On account of the untimely death of Venkatesh, the petitioners lost their earning member of the family and lost love and affection of the deceased.

It is the further case of the Petitioner in MVC No.927/2022 that, immediately after the accident he was shifted to Madakshira Government Hospital, provided first aid treatment then shifted to Sree Raghavendra Hospital,

The respondents being the RC owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence these petitions.
6. In response to the summons, the Respondent insurer has appeared in both the cases and filed written statement.

In spite of due service of summons the respondent RC owner did not appear hence, placed ex- parte.

this court has framed the following issues:

In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the Driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AA-8042, the Petitioner in MVC No.926/2022 has got examined 1st petitioner/Mother of the deceased as PW.1 and she filed affidavit in lieu of her chief examination and got marked Exs.P.1 to 7.
During her cross-examination nothing worthwhile is elicited.
The petitioner in MVC No.926/2022 got examined himself as PW.2 and filed affidavit in lieu of his chief examination and reiterated the contents of the petition averments.

During  SCCH - 25 10 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
 927/2022 his cross-examination, he has stated that the bike in which he was going belongs to his friend/deceased Venkatesh and that he has DL.
The Road was about 15ft wide.
There were no street lights.
He was sitting in the middle between the deceased and Narasappa.
Further admitted that the deceased tried to over taken the parked lorry, but a KSRTC bus came from the opposite direction and due to the headlights Venkatesh hit the parked Lorry.
His cousin Umesh gave the complaint to the police.
Both the petitioners have produced the police documents i.e., FIR, FIS, spot mahazar, spot sketch, MVA report, PM certificate and charge sheet as per Exs.P.1 to 7.
On perusal of documents it is clear that the accident occurred on 31.10.2021 and the FIR was registered on the next day 01.11.20221 at about 8.00 am at Ex.P.1.

sentences.text: Spot mahazar at Ex.P.3 was conducted on 01.11.2021.
The spot sketch at Ex.P.4 shows the accident spot.

As per the IMV report at Ex.P.5, there was no  SCCH - 25 11 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
 927/2022 damages to the Lorry and the Two wheeler was broken to its left indicator.
After investigation charge sheet is field against the driver of the Lorry by the police.
Other than the police documents, none of the other parties have produced any other documents contrary to these.

Therefore, on perusal of above documents, it is clear that the accident was caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of the Lorry bearing No.KA-51-AA-8042 in parking the Lorry in the middle of the Road without any indicators.
Accordingly, issue No.1 in MVC 927/2022 and Issue No.2 in MVC 926/2022 are held in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.1 in MVC No.926/2022
It is the case of the Petitioners that, the Petitioner No.1 is the Mother and Petitioner No.2 is the Father of the deceased Venkatesh.
The Petitioners to prove their relationship have examined the 1st Petitioner as Pw.1.
PW.1 has specifically spoken about the relationship in her chief- examination.

Apart from that, to prove the relationship, the  SCCH - 25 12 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
 927/2022 Petitioners have produced notarized copy of their Aadhar cards and the deceased Card as per Ex.P.11.

In the Aadhar Card of the deceased his father's name is mentioned as Vadde Narayanamma vs K. Sunitha on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148025627/
8 Narayanappa and in the Aadhar card of the petitioner No.1/mother's of the deceased her husband's name is mentioned as Narayanappa who is the father of the deceased and petitioner No.2.
In the Aadhar Cards of the petitioner No.2 his father name shown as Late Thimappa.
The petitioners have also produced Inquest Mahazar at Ex.P.12, it shows the name of the petitioner Nos.1 & 2 as mother and father of the deceased Venkatesh.
These documents are public documents and they have got initial presumptive value under law.
These documents have not been seriously disputed by the Respondents.
The Respondents have not produced any contrary documents to dispute and rebut the contents of documents produced by the Petitioners.
As such, there are no reasons to discard the oral and documentary evidence produced by the Petitioners.

Under such circumstances, relying upon the  SCCH - 25 13 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
 927/2022 oral evidence of Pw.1 and the documents, this court is of the opinion that the Petitioner Nos.1 & 2 are the mother and father of the deceased Venkatesh.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 in MVC 926/2022 is held in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.3 in MVC No.926/2022:

transportation of dead body, funeral expenses.

sentences.text: the Petitioners are entitled for compensation as per the following discussion.
Monthly income  15.
According to the Petitioners, the deceased was doing Mason work and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
In this regard, Petitioners have nor produced any documents nor examined any witness.
The accident was occurred in the year 2021.

Therefore, this court deems it fit  SCCH - 25 14 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
 927/2022 to fix the notional income of the deceased at Rs.15,000/-
per month.
Hence the same is considered as the monthly income of the deceased.
Age of the deceased  16.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced Aadhar Card of the deceased at Ex.P.11.
As per Ex.P.11 the deceased was aged about 26 years.
This is a public document and has got presumptive value under law.
This shows that as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased was 27 years.

Therefore,
his age is considered as 27 years.
(i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE  PROSPECTS:-

In so far as the Loss of dependency is concerned,
petitioner Nos.1 & 2 mother and father both are depending on the income of the deceased.
Therefore, both are considered as the dependents of the deceased.

As per the Vadde Narayanamma vs K. Sunitha on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148025627/
10 principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s  SCCH - 25 15 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
 927/2022 Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 17.
 17.
As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157) persons aged above 60 years are not entitled to any future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As mentioned above, since the deceased was under below 40 years age slab, 25% future prospects is to be added to his monthly income.

So Rs.3,750/- (Rs.15,000/- X 25% = Rs.3,750/-)
should be added to his monthly salary of Rs.15,000/- then it comes to Rs.18,750/- per month.
As per the Sarala Verma case, if the deceased is a bachelor, then 1/2 of his income has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses, balance comes to Rs.9,375/-.

Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.19,12,500/-
(Rs.9,375/- X 17 x 12) = Rs.19,12,500/-).

SCCH - 25 16 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
 927/2022  (ii) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:-

In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs.
Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130, the Hon'ble Apex court has observed  "Consortium" is a compendious term, which  encompasses spousal consortium, parental  consortium and filial consortium.

sentences.text: The Petitioner Nos.1 & 2 are the Mother and Father of the deceased.
Both have to live remaining part of their life in the absence of their Care taking Son.

The loss  SCCH - 25 17 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
 927/2022 of a Son full of hopes for the future can never be suitably compensated to the parents.
However, petitioner Nos.1 & 2 are entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- each and Rs.88,000/- under the head of loss of consortium.

(iii) TRANSPORTATION AND FUNERAL  EXPENSES AND LOSS OF ESTATE:-
 In so far as the funeral and transportation expenses are concerned, the Petitioners have contended that they have spent Rs.7,00,000/- towards medical expenses,
transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.

But,
there is no document produced in this regard.
In addition there are expenses during the death of a person for which documents cannot be maintained.
Therefore, in the interest of justice the Petitioners are awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

If the deceased was alive he would have certainly saved some amount out of his living Vadde Narayanamma vs K. Sunitha on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148025627/
12 and personal expenses and created an estate in favour of  SCCH - 25 18 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
 927/2022 the Petitioners.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of estate.
(iv) MEDICAL EXPENSES:-
In so far as the Medical expenses are concerned, the Petitioners have contended that they have spent Rs.7,00,000/- towards medical expenses.

In this regard,
the petitioners have produced 126 medical bills for Rs.5,62,817/-.
There is no contrary to these bills from the respondents.
Therefore, the petitioners are entitled Rs.5,62,817/- under the head of Medical Expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioners in MVC 926/2022 are entitled for a total sum of Rs.26,03,317/-.
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.26,03,500/-.
20. Issue No.2 in MVC No.927/2022:

In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced Discharge summary of Sriraghavendra Multispciality hospital at  SCCH - 25 19 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
 927/2022 Ex.P.13.
As per Ex.P.13 the Petitioner has suffered Left Hip Greater Trochantric Avulsion fracture.
21 . The petitioner has also got examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.15 & 16 clinical examination report and X-ray.

He has deposed the details of Vadde Narayanamma vs K. Sunitha on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148025627/
13 injuries and surgery undergone by the petitioner and diagnosed left greater trochanteric avulsion fracture and underwent surgery.
He further stated that the petitioner is suffering total disability of the left lower limb at 39% and to the whole body at 13%.
22. PW.3 in his cross examination has stated that he has not treated the petitioner.
At the time of discharge the petitioner's condition was stable.
He has not seen the followup records.
Fractures are united.
He does not require any further medical treatments.
Further, the petitioner does not suffer from any inability but has only some difficulties.

SCCH - 25 20 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
 927/2022  Disability:

23 . From the evidence of PW.3 and the documents on record, it is clear that the petitioner has suffered left greater throchanteric avulsion fracture, underwent ORIF with sutures and later discharged.
He has stated that he was doing Mason Work.
This means that he has to do the Mason work with his hand only and could not stand for a long time and do the work.
This kind of disability will affect his day to day work.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the whole body disability at 13%.

Monthly income:
 24.

The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that,
he was doing Mason Work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

In this regard he has not examined any witness nor Vadde Narayanamma vs K. Sunitha on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148025627/
14 produced any documents like Bank statement etc., to prove his earnings.
The accident occurred in the year 2021.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.15,000/- per month.
At the time of accident the  SCCH - 25 21 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
927/2022 Petitioner was aged about 27 years as could be made out from Ex.P.14/Aadhar Card.
He was hale and healthy before the accident.

Keeping all the above things in mind,
Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:-
 i) PAIN
AND SUFFERING:-

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Madakshira Govt. Hospital, provided first aid and thereafter he was shifted to Raghavendra Hospital, Hindupur, wherein he was admitted and treated as an inpatient from 10.11.2021 to 16.11.2021 was diagnosed and underwent surgery which can be made out from Ex.P.13.
Considering that the nature of injury he has undergone are grievous, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.80,000/- under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines, conveyance,
food and nourishment and other incidental expenses etc.

In  SCCH - 25 22 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
 927/2022 this regard, he has not produced any medical bills.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled any amount under this head.
Vadde Narayanamma vs K. Sunitha on 12 November, 2024

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148025627/
15  iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:-
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary of Sri Raghavendra Multispecialty Hospital to show the duration and treatment in the said hospital.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least One month time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.15,000/- under this head.

iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:-
 On perusal of Ex.P.14/Notarized copy of Aadhar Card of the petitioner, his year of birth is mentioned as 1994.
The accident occurred on 31.10.2021.

Therefore, as on the date  SCCH - 25 23 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
 927/2022 of the accident the Petitioner's age is 27 years.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 17.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.3,97,800/-
(Rs.15,000/- x 12 x 17 x 13%= Rs.3,97,800/-) under this head.
(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:-
The Petitioner was aged about 27 years at the time of accident.

He has sustained grievous injuries and as per Vadde Narayanamma vs K. Sunitha on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148025627/
16 consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 10%
functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.

Therefore,
considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.

SCCH - 25 24 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
 927/2022  (vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND  NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospital, admitted as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

25. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.80,000/-
2. Medical expenses -- NIL-- 3. Loss of income during laid up period Rs.15,000/-
4. Loss of future income Rs.3,97,800/-
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/-
 happiness 6.

Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/-
 nourishment charges

TOTAL Rs.5,32,800/-

LIABILITY:
 26.
The respondents did not prove their defence.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The respondent insurance company of the Lorry is liable to indemnify the respondent Owner.

The petitioners in MVC No.926/2022 have claimed for a sum of Rs.40,00,000/- but they are entitled only for a sum of Rs.26,03,500/- with interest @6%
per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

The petitioner in MVC No.927/2022 has claimed for a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.5,33,000/- with interest @6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, issue No.3 in MVC No.926/2022 and Issue No.2 in MVC No.927/2022 are held in the Affirmative.

 ORDER
The petitions in MVC No.926/2022 & MVC No.927/2022 are hereby allowed with cost.

However, the Respondent No.2 being insurer is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1 and directed to deposit the compensation amount to the Petitioners within 60 days from today.

The Petitioners in MVC No.926/2022 are entitled for a sum of Rs.26,03,500/- (Rupees Twenty Six Lakhs Three Thousand AND Five SCCH - 25 27 MVC Nos.926/2022 & 927/2022 Hundred only)
with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of filing till the date of depositing the award amount.

The Petitioner in MVC No.927/2022 is entitled for a sum of Rs.5,33,000/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Thirty Three Thousand only) with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of filing till the date of depositing the award amount.

 Common Judgment
The Petitioners in MVC No.926/2022 and MVC No.927/2022 have filed these petitions u/Sec.166 of MV Act  SCCH - 25 3 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
 927/2022 seeking compensation for the death of their son Mr.Venkatesh and for the injuries sustained by him in an RTA.
opennyai_summary.facts:
The Doctor operated on the head injury and Mr.Venkatesh died on 27.11.2021 and the post mortem was conducted, body handed over to the petitioners.
At the time of accident, the deceased Venkatesh was doing Mason Work and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earning towards his family needs and welfare.
On account of the untimely death of Venkatesh, the petitioners lost their earning member of the family and lost love and affection of the deceased.
At the time of accident, he was doing Mortar Work and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries,
he cannot do his work and lost his income, future prospective life, happiness, earning capacity and has become disabled and dependant.
opennyai_summary.issue:
8. On the above rival contentions of the parties,
this court has framed the following issues:
 MVC No.926/2022  1.
Whether the petitioners prove that, they  are the legal heirs of the deceased  Sri.Venkatesh?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that, Sri.
 Venkatesh had died due to the injuries  sustained in the Road traffic accident that  occurred on 31.10.2021 at about 7.30pm,
 near Amidalagondi Village, Madakshira,
 Andrapradesha District, due to rash and  negligent driving of driver of Lorry bearing  Reg.No.KA-51-AA-8042 as alleged?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for  compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
4. What order or Award?
 MVC No.927/2022  1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, the  accident occurred on 31.10.2021 at 7.30pm  due to rash and negligent driving by the  driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AA-  SCCH - 25 8 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
Vadde Narayanamma vs K. Sunitha on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148025627/
5  927/2022  8042 and in the said accident petitioner  sustained injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for  compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
 3. What order or Award?
 9.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
After investigation charge sheet is field against the driver of the Lorry by the police.
Therefore, on perusal of above documents, it is clear that the accident was caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of the Lorry bearing No.KA-51-AA-8042 in parking the Lorry in the middle of the Road without any indicators.
As such, there are no reasons to discard the oral and documentary evidence produced by the Petitioners.
The accident was occurred in the year 2021.
Therefore, this court deems it fit  SCCH - 25 14 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
 927/2022 to fix the notional income of the deceased at Rs.15,000/-
per month.
Hence the same is considered as the monthly income of the deceased.
Age of the deceased  16.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced Aadhar Card of the deceased at Ex.P.11.
As per Ex.P.11 the deceased was aged about 26 years.
This is a public document and has got presumptive value under law.
This shows that as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased was 27 years.
Therefore,
his age is considered as 27 years.
(i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE  PROSPECTS:-
In so far as the Loss of dependency is concerned,
petitioner Nos.1 & 2 mother and father both are depending on the income of the deceased.
Therefore, both are considered as the dependents of the deceased.
As per the Vadde Narayanamma vs K. Sunitha on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148025627/
10 principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s  SCCH - 25 15 MVC Nos.926/2022 &
 927/2022 Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 17.
 17.
As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157) persons aged above 60 years are not entitled to any future prospects.
As mentioned above, since the deceased was under below 40 years age slab, 25% future prospects is to be added to his monthly income.
He has sustained grievous injuries and as per Vadde Narayanamma vs K. Sunitha on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148025627/
16 consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 10%
functional disability.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, in the interest of justice the Petitioners are awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of estate.
Therefore,
considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
25. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.80,000/-
2. Medical expenses -- NIL-- 3. Loss of income during laid up period Rs.15,000/-
4. Loss of future income Rs.3,97,800/-
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/-
 happiness 6.
Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/-
 nourishment charges
awarded to the Petitioner.
LIABILITY:
 26.
The respondents did not prove their defence.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The respondent insurance company of the Lorry is liable to indemnify the respondent Owner.
The petitioners in MVC No.926/2022 have claimed for a sum of Rs.40,00,000/- but they are entitled only for a sum of Rs.26,03,500/- with interest @6%
per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The petitioner in MVC No.927/2022 has claimed for a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.5,33,000/- with interest @6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, issue No.3 in MVC No.926/2022 and Issue No.2 in MVC No.927/2022 are held in the Affirmative.
For the reasons and discussions made above and  findings to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to  pass the following:-
 ORDER
The petitions in MVC No.926/2022 & MVC No.927/2022 are hereby allowed with cost.
The Respondent Nos.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
However, the Respondent No.2 being insurer is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1 and directed to deposit the compensation amount to the Petitioners within 60 days from today.
The Petitioners in MVC No.926/2022 are entitled for a sum of Rs.26,03,500/- (Rupees Twenty Six Lakhs Three Thousand AND Five SCCH - 25 27 MVC Nos.926/2022 & 927/2022 Hundred only)
with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of filing till the date of depositing the award amount.
On deposit of compensation and interest, Rs.5,00,000/- each shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner Nos.1 & 2 for a period of 3 years in any Bank of their choice and remaining amount shall be released to the petitioner Nos.1 & 2 equally by way of e-payment with due acknowledgment and proper identification.
The Petitioner in MVC No.927/2022 is entitled for a sum of Rs.5,33,000/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Thirty Three Thousand only) with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of filing till the date of depositing the award amount.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released to SCCH - 25 28 MVC Nos.926/2022 & 927/2022 the petitioner by way of e-payment with due acknowledgment and proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/- in each case.
The original copy of this judgment is ordered to be kept in MVC No.926/2021 and copy shall be kept in MVC No.927/2021.
